plans.title: Fix alembic migration TypeError: Union descriptor __getitem__ (Python 3.14 + SQLAlchemy 2.0.36)
plans.purpose: Fix alembic upgrade head TypeError caused by PEP 604 union syntax (str | None) in SQLAlchemy models incompatible with Python 3.14 runtime.
learnings: When SQLAlchemy declarative models raise TypeError: descriptor '__getitem__' requires a 'typing.Union' object but received a 'tuple' on Python 3.14, the fix is NOT rewriting `X | None` to `Optional[X]` (both trigger the same code path) — it's upgrading the sqlalchemy pin. SQLAlchemy 2.0.36 predates Python 3.14 support; support began at 2.0.41 with further annotation fixes through later 2.0.x patches. Always check runtime Python version against library's supported-version history first for this class of typing/annotation errors.

steps.verification: Manual review of both Dockerfiles confirms shell-form CMD with exec prefix on the final long-running process. plans.scope_in: Backend only: add `background_tasks: BackgroundTasks` param to every route function that calls send_email(), and change each direct send_email(...) call to background_tasks.add_task(send_email, ...). Covers auth.py (_send_mfa_otp_email helper + its 2 callers), collaborations.py (send + respond), projects.py (invite + respond), publications.py (review), reviewer_assignments.py (create assignment).
plans.scope_out: Not touching create_notification() (DB-only, already fast). Not switching SMTP provider/credentials. Not adding a task queue/Celery -- BackgroundTasks is sufficient since this is single-process uvicorn. No frontend changes needed.
plans.why: Root cause found: backend/app/core/email.py's send_email() opens a real smtplib.SMTP connection to smtp.gmail.com synchronously inside the request handler (backend/app/api/routes/collaborations.py send_collaboration_request), with its own 10s socket timeout -- coincidentally identical to the frontend's requests.post(timeout=10) to the backend. When Gmail SMTP is slow/unreachable from this machine's network, the backend request blocks near 10s and the frontend times out first, surfacing as a 500 with ReadTimeoutError. The docstring on send_email already promises 'fire-and-forget, never let it affect the HTTP response' but the code doesn't honor that -- it's called inline, not backgrounded. The same blocking pattern exists at 8 call sites across 5 route files (auth.py x2, projects.py x2, collaborations.py x3, publications.py x1, reviewer_assignments.py x1), so any of those requests (MFA login/resend, forgot-password, project invite/respond, publication review) can hit the same failure whenever SMTP is slow. Fix: move every send_email(...) call onto FastAPI's BackgroundTasks so it runs after the HTTP response is already sent, never blocking the caller.
